solved_examples.title: Standard Placement Problem on Series Completion
solved_examples.question: If an item is marked at Rs. 1,200 and sold after two successive discounts of 10% and 20%, what is the net selling price?
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Single equivalent discount = d1 + d2 - (d1 * d2 / 100)% = 10 + 20 - (10 * 20 / 100)% = 30 - 2 = 28%.

solved_examples.title: Efficiency & Work Ratio Problem on Series Completion
solved_examples.question: Worker A can complete a task in 12 days and Worker B can complete the same task in 18 days. If they work on alternate days starting with A, in how many days will the work be completed?
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Assume Total Work = LCM(12, 18) = 36 units.
Step 2: A's 1-day work = 36 / 12 = 3 units/day. B's 1-day work = 36 / 18 = 2 units/day.
Step 3: In a 2-day cycle (Day 1: A, Day 2: B), total work done = 3 + 2 = 5 units.
Step 4: Number of complete cycles in 36 units = 36 // 5 = 7 cycles (14 days), completing 7 * 5 = 35 units.
Step 5: Remaining work = 36 - 35 = 1 unit. Day 15 is A's turn (efficiency 3 units/day). Time taken by A = 1/3 day.
Step 6: Total days = 14 + 1/3 = 14 1/3 days (or 14.33 days).

solved_examples.title: Speed & Relative Distance Problem on Series Completion
solved_examples.question: Two stations X and Y are 390 km apart. A train starts from X at 10 AM heading towards Y at 65 km/hr. Another train starts from Y at 11 AM heading towards X at 35 km/hr. At what time will they meet?
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Standardize start time to 11 AM. Distance covered by Train 1 from 10 AM to 11 AM (1 hour) = 65 km * 1 = 65 km.
Step 2: Remaining distance between trains at 11 AM = 390 - 65 = 325 km.
Step 3: Relative speed in opposite directions = 65 + 35 = 100 km/hr.
Step 4: Time taken to meet after 11 AM = Remaining Distance / Relative Speed = 325 / 100 = 3.25 hours = 3 hours 15 minutes.
Step 5: Meeting time = 11:00 AM + 3 hours 15 minutes = 2:15 PM.

solved_examples.title: Combinatorics & Probability Problem on Series Completion
solved_examples.question: A bag contains 5 red balls and 4 blue balls. If 3 balls are drawn at random without replacement, what is the probability that exactly 2 are red and 1 is blue?
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Total balls in bag = 5 + 4 = 9 balls. Total ways to choose 3 balls, n(S) = 9C3 = (9 * 8 * 7) / (3 * 2 * 1) = 84.
Step 2: Favorable ways to choose 2 red balls from 5 red = 5C2 = (5 * 4) / (2 * 1) = 10.
Step 3: Favorable ways to choose 1 blue ball from 4 blue = 4C1 = 4.
Step 4: Total favorable outcomes, n(E) = 5C2 * 4C1 = 10 * 4 = 40.
Step 5: Required Probability = n(E) / n(S) = 40 / 84 = 10 / 21.

options.A: Statements I and II together are not sufficient

mcqs.explanation: From I: R > P > Q. From II: P > S. We know R is taller than P, Q, S, but we do not know if S is taller than Q. However, R is clearly taller than P, and P is taller than both Q and S. Thus R is the tallest! Both statements together are sufficient.

mcqs.question: Question: What is the profit percentage earned by selling an article? Statement I: The article was sold for Rs. 600. Statement II: The marked price was Rs. 750.

options.A: Statements I and II together are not sufficient

mcqs.explanation: Profit percentage requires knowing Cost Price (CP). Neither statement provides CP or markup percentage over CP.

mcqs.question: Question: Is x > y? Statement I: x - y > 0. Statement II: x / y > 1.
mcqs.explanation: From I: x - y > 0 directly implies x > y for all real numbers. Statement II can be ambiguous if y is negative (e.g. x=-4, y=-2 gives 2 > 1 but x < y). Statement I alone is sufficient.

mcqs.question: Question: How much money did Rohan invest in compound interest? Statement I: The sum amounts to Rs. 1,210 in 2 years. Statement II: The annual compound interest rate is 10%.
mcqs.explanation: Amount = P * (1 + R/100)^T => 1,210 = P * (1.10)^2 => P = 1,210 / 1.21 = Rs. 1,000. Both together are sufficient.

solved_examples.question: A student scores 75% on an initial diagnostic test and subsequently improves by 20% on the final assessment. If the maximum marks were 200, find the student's final score.

solved_examples.title: Standard Placement Problem on Cube & Dice
solved_examples.question: If an item is marked at Rs. 1,200 and sold after two successive discounts of 10% and 20%, what is the net selling price?
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Single equivalent discount = d1 + d2 - (d1 * d2 / 100)% = 10 + 20 - (10 * 20 / 100)% = 30 - 2 = 28%.
Step 2: Selling price = Marked Price * (1 - Equivalent Discount / 100).
Verification: After 10% discount on 1200 = 1200 - 120 = 1080. After 20% discount on 1080 = 1080 - 216 = Rs. 864.

solved_examples.title: Efficiency & Work Ratio Problem on Cube & Dice
solved_examples.question: Worker A can complete a task in 12 days and Worker B can complete the same task in 18 days. If they work on alternate days starting with A, in how many days will the work be completed?
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Assume Total Work = LCM(12, 18) = 36 units.
Step 2: A's 1-day work = 36 / 12 = 3 units/day. B's 1-day work = 36 / 18 = 2 units/day.
Step 3: In a 2-day cycle (Day 1: A, Day 2: B), total work done = 3 + 2 = 5 units.
Step 4: Number of complete cycles in 36 units = 36 // 5 = 7 cycles (14 days), completing 7 * 5 = 35 units.
Step 5: Remaining work = 36 - 35 = 1 unit. Day 15 is A's turn (efficiency 3 units/day). Time taken by A = 1/3 day.
Step 6: Total days = 14 + 1/3 = 14 1/3 days (or 14.33 days).

solved_examples.title: Speed & Relative Distance Problem on Cube & Dice
solved_examples.question: Two stations X and Y are 390 km apart. A train starts from X at 10 AM heading towards Y at 65 km/hr. Another train starts from Y at 11 AM heading towards X at 35 km/hr. At what time will they meet?
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Standardize start time to 11 AM. Distance covered by Train 1 from 10 AM to 11 AM (1 hour) = 65 km * 1 = 65 km.
Step 2: Remaining distance between trains at 11 AM = 390 - 65 = 325 km.
Step 3: Relative speed in opposite directions = 65 + 35 = 100 km/hr.
Step 4: Time taken to meet after 11 AM = Remaining Distance / Relative Speed = 325 / 100 = 3.25 hours = 3 hours 15 minutes.
Step 5: Meeting time = 11:00 AM + 3 hours 15 minutes = 2:15 PM.

solved_examples.title: Combinatorics & Probability Problem on Cube & Dice
solved_examples.question: A bag contains 5 red balls and 4 blue balls. If 3 balls are drawn at random without replacement, what is the probability that exactly 2 are red and 1 is blue?
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Total balls in bag = 5 + 4 = 9 balls. Total ways to choose 3 balls, n(S) = 9C3 = (9 * 8 * 7) / (3 * 2 * 1) = 84.
Step 2: Favorable ways to choose 2 red balls from 5 red = 5C2 = (5 * 4) / (2 * 1) = 10.
Step 3: Favorable ways to choose 1 blue ball from 4 blue = 4C1 = 4.
Step 4: Total favorable outcomes, n(E) = 5C2 * 4C1 = 10 * 4 = 40.
Step 5: Required Probability = n(E) / n(S) = 40 / 84 = 10 / 21.

mcqs.explanation: Two painted faces occur along the edges: formula = 12 * (n - 2) where n = 4/1 = 4. Count = 12 * (4 - 2) = 12 * 2 = 24 cubes.

mcqs.question: In the above 4 cm painted cube, how many smaller 1 cm cubes have NO painted faces (zero painted)?
mcqs.explanation: Zero painted faces form the internal core: formula = (n - 2)^3 = (4 - 2)^3 = 2^3 = 8 cubes.

mcqs.question: How many smaller cubes in the 4 cm cube have exactly THREE painted faces?
mcqs.explanation: Three painted faces are located exclusively at the 8 vertices of the cube. The answer is always 8.

mcqs.question: How many smaller cubes have exactly ONE painted face?
mcqs.explanation: One painted face occurs on the faces: formula = 6 * (n - 2)^2 = 6 * (4 - 2)^2 = 6 * 4 = 24 cubes.

mcqs.question: Two positions of a dice are shown. In position 1: top 1, front 2, right 3. In position 2: top 1, front 5, right 6. Which number is opposite 1?
mcqs.explanation: The numbers adjacent to 1 are 2, 3, 5, 6. The only remaining number that can be opposite 1 is 4.

mcqs.question: A cube painted yellow on all faces is cut into 125 small cubes of equal size. How many cubes have at least one face painted?
mcqs.explanation: n = 125^(1/3) = 5. Unpainted cubes = (5 - 2)^3 = 3^3 = 27. Cubes with at least one painted face = Total - Unpainted = 125 - 27 = 98.

mcqs.question: If a dice is rolled, what is the probability of rolling a composite number?
mcqs.explanation: Faces are {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. Composite numbers are 4 and 6 (2 outcomes). Probability = 2/6 = 1/3.

mcqs.question: When a flat cardboard pattern is folded into a cube, if opposite faces never touch, which face is opposite face A in layout A-B-C-D in a row with E on top of B and F below B?
mcqs.explanation: In linear strip of faces, alternate faces are opposite: A is opposite C, B is opposite D, and flap E is opposite flap F.

mcqs.explanation: 3 must be opposite 4. Therefore, the four faces adjacent to 3 are 1, 6, 2, and 5.

solved_examples.title: Efficiency & Work Ratio Problem on Para Jumbles
solved_examples.question: Worker A can complete a task in 12 days and Worker B can complete the same task in 18 days. If they work on alternate days starting with A, in how many days will the work be completed?
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Assume Total Work = LCM(12, 18) = 36 units.
Step 2: A's 1-day work = 36 / 12 = 3 units/day. B's 1-day work = 36 / 18 = 2 units/day.
Step 3: In a 2-day cycle (Day 1: A, Day 2: B), total work done = 3 + 2 = 5 units.
Step 4: Number of complete cycles in 36 units = 36 // 5 = 7 cycles (14 days), completing 7 * 5 = 35 units.

solved_examples.title: Speed & Relative Distance Problem on Para Jumbles

step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Standardize start time to 11 AM. Distance covered by Train 1 from 10 AM to 11 AM (1 hour) = 65 km * 1 = 65 km.

Step 3: Relative speed in opposite directions = 65 + 35 = 100 km/hr.

solved_examples.question: A bag contains 5 red balls and 4 blue balls. If 3 balls are drawn at random without replacement, what is the probability that exactly 2 are red and 1 is blue?
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Total balls in bag = 5 + 4 = 9 balls. Total ways to choose 3 balls, n(S) = 9C3 = (9 * 8 * 7) / (3 * 2 * 1) = 84.

options.B: CPUs cannot process more than two instructions simultaneously

options.B: Two servers can always agree in 2 network hops

options.B: Fiber optic cables transmit data instantaneously
options.D: Local method calls are slower than remote APIs

mcqs.explanation: Network latency is non-zero; treating remote calls as local in-memory invocations causes hanging threads and cascading system outages.

mcqs.question: In concurrency analysis, what is a 'Race Condition'?

options.B: A benchmarking competition between two different algorithms
options.C: A network cable transmitting data too quickly
options.D: A database running out of disk space

mcqs.explanation: A race condition occurs when concurrent threads access shared state without proper synchronization, making output non-deterministic.

mcqs.question: What is the primary cause of 'Cache Invalidation' being considered one of the hardest problems in computer science?

options.B: RAM chips frequently lose physical power
options.C: CPUs do not have internal registers
options.D: Operating systems delete cache files every minute

mcqs.explanation: Keeping distributed cache copies strictly synchronized with evolving underlying databases involves complex timing and distributed state trade-offs.

mcqs.question: Why is 'Premature Optimization' described by Donald Knuth as 'the root of all evil'?

options.A: Developers spend critical time optimizing uncritical micro-paths, introducing bugs and complexity before measuring real bottlenecks
options.C: Optimized code runs slower than unoptimized code
options.D: Computers do not need fast code

mcqs.explanation: Knuth noted that ~97% of run time is spent in tiny code pockets. Optimizing everything early complicates architecture without measurable gains.

mcqs.question: What architectural objective does 'Idempotency' achieve in RESTful API design?

options.A: Guaranteeing that executing the same request multiple times produces the identical side-effect as executing it once
options.C: Forcing all API requests to use HTTP GET

mcqs.explanation: Idempotency ensures that accidental duplicate API retries (e.g., payment submissions) do not cause duplicate state mutations.

mcqs.question: In software reliability engineering, what does 'Graceful Degradation' mean?

options.A: A system's ability to maintain core functionality at reduced performance during partial subsystem failures rather than crashing entirely
options.C: Software deleting user data when an error occurs
options.D: Shutting down the entire data center immediately

mcqs.explanation: Graceful degradation ensures that if a secondary service (e.g., recommendation engine) fails, primary workflows (e.g., checkout) remain operational.

mcqs.question: Pointing to a man, a woman said, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the woman related to the man?
mcqs.explanation: 'Only daughter of my mother' is the woman herself. The man's mother is the woman, so the woman is his mother.

mcqs.question: Which number replaces the question mark in the matrix: [2, 3, 5], [9, 4, 40], [4, 5, ?]
mcqs.explanation: Row logic: (col1 * col2) - 1 for row 1: 2*3 - 1 = 5. Row 2: (9 * 4) + 4 = 40. Or row 1: 2^2 + 1 = 5; 3^2 - 4... Direct formula: col1^2 + col2 = 4 + 5... Alternatively: col1 * col2 + 1 = 2*3-1=5, 4*5+1=21.

mcqs.question: In an office, 70% of staff drink coffee, 60% drink tea, and every employee drinks at least one of the two. If 30 employees drink both, what is total staff?
mcqs.explanation: % drinking both = 70% + 60% - 100% = 30%. If 30% = 30 employees, total staff = 100.

mcqs.question: If 'REASON' is coded as 5 and 'BELIEVED' as 7, what is the code for 'GOVERNMENT'?
mcqs.explanation: Code = Number of letters in the word minus 1. REASON has 6 letters -> 5. BELIEVED has 8 letters -> 7. GOVERNMENT has 10 letters -> 10 - 1 = 9.

solved_examples.title: Foundation Problem on All Recruiters
solved_examples.question: A student scores 75% on an initial diagnostic test and subsequently improves by 20% on the final assessment. If the maximum marks were 200, find the student's final score.
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Calculate initial score = 75% of 200 = (75 / 100) * 200 = 150 marks.
Step 2: Improvement factor = 20% increase on initial score.
Step 3: Score increase = 20% of 150 = (20 / 100) * 150 = 30 marks.
Step 4: Final score = 150 + 30 = 180 marks out of 200 (or 90%).
Speed Check: Direct factor = 200 * 0.75 * 1.20 = 200 * 0.90 = 180 marks.

solved_examples.title: Standard Placement Problem on All Recruiters
solved_examples.question: If an item is marked at Rs. 1,200 and sold after two successive discounts of 10% and 20%, what is the net selling price?
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Single equivalent discount = d1 + d2 - (d1 * d2 / 100)% = 10 + 20 - (10 * 20 / 100)% = 30 - 2 = 28%.
Step 2: Selling price = Marked Price * (1 - Equivalent Discount / 100).
Verification: After 10% discount on 1200 = 1200 - 120 = 1080. After 20% discount on 1080 = 1080 - 216 = Rs. 864.

solved_examples.title: Efficiency & Work Ratio Problem on All Recruiters
solved_examples.question: Worker A can complete a task in 12 days and Worker B can complete the same task in 18 days. If they work on alternate days starting with A, in how many days will the work be completed?
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Assume Total Work = LCM(12, 18) = 36 units.
Step 2: A's 1-day work = 36 / 12 = 3 units/day. B's 1-day work = 36 / 18 = 2 units/day.
Step 3: In a 2-day cycle (Day 1: A, Day 2: B), total work done = 3 + 2 = 5 units.
Step 4: Number of complete cycles in 36 units = 36 // 5 = 7 cycles (14 days), completing 7 * 5 = 35 units.
Step 5: Remaining work = 36 - 35 = 1 unit. Day 15 is A's turn (efficiency 3 units/day). Time taken by A = 1/3 day.
Step 6: Total days = 14 + 1/3 = 14 1/3 days (or 14.33 days).

solved_examples.title: Speed & Relative Distance Problem on All Recruiters
solved_examples.question: Two stations X and Y are 390 km apart. A train starts from X at 10 AM heading towards Y at 65 km/hr. Another train starts from Y at 11 AM heading towards X at 35 km/hr. At what time will they meet?
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Standardize start time to 11 AM. Distance covered by Train 1 from 10 AM to 11 AM (1 hour) = 65 km * 1 = 65 km.
Step 2: Remaining distance between trains at 11 AM = 390 - 65 = 325 km.
Step 3: Relative speed in opposite directions = 65 + 35 = 100 km/hr.
Step 4: Time taken to meet after 11 AM = Remaining Distance / Relative Speed = 325 / 100 = 3.25 hours = 3 hours 15 minutes.
Step 5: Meeting time = 11:00 AM + 3 hours 15 minutes = 2:15 PM.

solved_examples.title: Combinatorics & Probability Problem on All Recruiters
solved_examples.question: A bag contains 5 red balls and 4 blue balls. If 3 balls are drawn at random without replacement, what is the probability that exactly 2 are red and 1 is blue?
step_by_step_solution: Step 1: Total balls in bag = 5 + 4 = 9 balls. Total ways to choose 3 balls, n(S) = 9C3 = (9 * 8 * 7) / (3 * 2 * 1) = 84.
Step 2: Favorable ways to choose 2 red balls from 5 red = 5C2 = (5 * 4) / (2 * 1) = 10.
Step 3: Favorable ways to choose 1 blue ball from 4 blue = 4C1 = 4.
Step 4: Total favorable outcomes, n(E) = 5C2 * 4C1 = 10 * 4 = 40.
Step 5: Required Probability = n(E) / n(S) = 40 / 84 = 10 / 21.

mcqs.question: A can complete a project in 18 days, B in 24 days, and C in 36 days. They all work together for 4 days, then A leaves. B and C continue for 2 more days, then B leaves. How many days does C take to finish the rest?
mcqs.explanation: LCM(18, 24, 36) = 72 units. A=4, B=3, C=2. In 4 days A+B+C do 4*9 = 36 units. In next 2 days B+C do 2*5 = 10 units. Total done = 46 units. Remaining = 26 units. C alone takes 26 / 2 = 13 (approx 14 days with step boundaries).

mcqs.explanation: Relative speed = 72 - 54 = 18 km/hr = 18 * (5/18) = 5 m/s. Time to gain 150 m = 150 / 5 = 30 seconds.

mcqs.question: A dishonest milkman buys milk at Rs. 24 per liter and adds 25% water. He sells the mixture at Rs. 27 per liter. What is his total profit percentage?
mcqs.explanation: Assume 4 L milk bought for 4 * 24 = Rs. 96. Adds 1 L water (25%) -> 5 L mixture. SP = 5 * 27 = Rs. 135. Profit = 135 - 96 = Rs. 39. Profit % = (39 / 96) * 100% = 40.625%.

mcqs.question: What is the remainder when (1! + 2! + 3! + ... + 100!) is divided by 12?
mcqs.explanation: 4! = 24, which is divisible by 12. All subsequent factorials (5!, 6!... 100!) contain 4! and are divisible by 12. Remainder = (1! + 2! + 3!) mod 12 = (1 + 2 + 6) mod 12 = 9 mod 12 = 9.

mcqs.question: How many words can be formed from the letters of the word 'CAMPUS' such that no two vowels are adjacent?
mcqs.explanation: Consonants: C, M, P, S (4 consonants). Arrange consonants in 4! = 24 ways. They create 5 gaps: _ C _ M _ P _ S _. Place 2 vowels (A, U) into 5 gaps: 5P2 = 20 ways. Total words = 24 * 20 = 480.

mcqs.question: A box contains 3 black, 4 white, and 5 red balls. If two balls are drawn at random without replacement, what is the probability that both are of different colors?
mcqs.explanation: Total balls = 12. P(same color) = (3C2 + 4C2 + 5C2) / 12C2 = (3 + 6 + 10) / 66 = 19/66. P(different colors) = 1 - 19/66 = 47/66.

mcqs.question: A clock loses 5 minutes every day. If it is set correctly at 12:00 noon on Monday, what time will it display at 12:00 noon on the following Monday?
mcqs.explanation: 7 days elapse. Total loss = 7 * 5 = 35 minutes. Clock displays 12:00 - 35 mins = 11:25 AM.

mcqs.question: In a row of boys facing North, A is 13th from left and D is 17th from right. If A is 11th from right, what is D's position from the left end?
mcqs.explanation: Total boys = A's left + A's right - 1 = 13 + 11 - 1 = 23. D's position from left = Total - D's right + 1 = 23 - 17 + 1 = 7th.

mcqs.question: What is the maximum number of points of intersection of 8 distinct straight lines and 4 distinct circles in a plane?
mcqs.explanation: Line-line intersections: 8C2 * 1 = 28. Circle-circle intersections: 4C2 * 2 = 6 * 2 = 12. Line-circle intersections: (8 * 4) * 2 = 64. Total = 28 + 12 + 64 = 104 (or with tangencies 114 max theoretical).
